10.1002_adfm.202508730: Electrocatalytic water splitting stands as a pivotal technology for the large‐scale production of high‐purity hydrogen, with the central challenge residing in the development of efficient, stable, and cost‐effective hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalysts. This study proposes a simple, room‐temperature stirring method (2 h) developed to anchor [RuCl] 2+ onto carboxyl‐functionalized carbon nanotubes (CNT‐COOH). During the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), partial Cl⁻ desorption under reductive potentials triggers the in situ formation of Cl‐modified Ru (100) nanoparticles. Localized Cl⁻ coordination induces redistribution of surface electronic states and mitigation site‐blocking effects, activating the traditionally inert (100) facets through optimization of Ru electronic states, thereby surpassing the activity of conventionally synthesized Ru/CNT(101) (prepared via pyrolysis). The self‐optimized Ru/CNT(Cl‐100) demonstrated exceptional mass activity (6.47 A mg Ru ⁻¹ at η = 50 mV) and sustained stability, outperforming most reported Ru‐based catalysts. This work highlights a ligand‐mediated strategy to unlock the latent catalytic potential of low‐index facets, providing a scalable pathway for high‐performance HER systems.
10.1002_adfm.76938: The green and sustainable recycling of spent graphite (SG) is crucial for the circular economy of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), yet remains notoriously challenging due to the severe structural degradation and unstable electrode/electrolyte interface. Traditional recycling methods, such as high‐temperature treatment and leaching‐calcination, are often energy‐intensive and environmentally destructive. Herein, a direct and rapid revival strategy with microwave is proposed, which accomplishes the conformal construction of an elastic rippled carbon nanoskin on the surface of SG. The carbon nanoskin effectively repairs the microcracks and defects, and its unique elastic rippled structure accommodates the cyclic volume variation upon lithiation/delithiation, which ensures the stable interface and excellent performance. The regenerated graphite delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 87.57%, a reversible capacity of 370.32 mAh g −1 after 400 cycles at 0.5 C with a capacity retention of 99.86%, and an outstanding rate performance with a capacity of 257.28 mAh g −1 after 450 cycles at 2 C, which is superior to commercial graphite. It also exhibits a notable performance in LiCoO 2 and LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cells. This work reveals a novel mechanistic insight into graphite regeneration through interfacial mechanical protection, offering a scalable and efficient pathway for upcycling spent graphite into advanced anode products.
10.1016_j.memsci.2026.125541: Single-pass tangential flow filtration (SPTFF) is an enabling technology for continuous bioprocessing, but its performance can be limited by membrane fouling at high protein concentrations. In this work, we investigate fouling mechanisms and critical flux using whey protein isolate (WPI) as a model protein and compare the results to a monoclonal antibody (mAb). Batch tangential flow filtration (TFF) experiments were performed under flux-stepping and pressure-stepping conditions to determine the critical flux of both protein systems over a range of concentrations. The critical flux declined significantly with increasing feed concentration for both WPI and mAb solutions, in agreement with the concentration polarisation model. Despite structural and molecular size differences between WPI and the mAb, their critical flux behaviour and gel concentration were remarkably similar, supporting the use of WPI as a surrogate in early-stage studies. The translation of batch TFF findings to SPTFF was also assessed. At low fluxes, fouling was dominated by a pore blocking mechanism. At higher fluxes, fouling severity increased beyond the critical flux, as concentration polarisation and cake layer formation became dominant. The data could be fitted to Hermia’s blocking laws, but more sophisticated models are needed to account for the changes in protein concentrations over both time and membrane length during the initial periods of operation. Overall, this study highlights both the strengths and limitations of WPI as a model protein and provides guidance for optimizing filtration strategies in therapeutic antibody manufacturing. • Concentration polarisation model shows similar results for whey proteins and a monoclonal antibody • Batch critical flux data predicts fouling onset in constant flux SPTFF • Changes in transmembrane pressure predicted by pore blockage and cake filtration models • Whey protein is validated as a low-cost surrogate in early SPTFF fouling studies
10.1021_acs.analchem.6c01581: Both sluggish charge transfer and rapid recombination of photogenerated carriers lead to low photoelectric conversion efficiency, still presenting challenges for the photoelectrochemical (PEC) immunoassay. Herein, an innovative PEC sensing platform was proposed based on hollow surface immobilized SnS 2 –ZnIn 2 S 4 shell-ZnS core (SnS 2 /ZIS@ZnS) heterojunctions with a tandem built-in electric field (BIEF). To begin with, Sn(IV)-ZIS@ZnS featuring a hollow core–shell structure was fabricated via lateral epitaxy and adsorption methods. Following the release of H 2 S, after carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) was specifically recognized via a sandwich-type immune reaction, the released H 2 S reacted with Sn(IV)-ZIS@ZnS to form dual S-scheme heterojunction SnS 2 /ZIS@ZnS. Owing to the inherent differences in work function among these three heterocomponents, a tandem BIEF was established within the heterojunction. The tandem BIEF effectively facilitated charge transfer and enhanced the photoelectric conversion efficiency, ultimately enhancing the photocurrent signal. Benefiting from the pronounced variation in photocurrent, the proposed PEC sensing platform enables highly sensitive detection of CEA, exhibiting a linear detection range from 0.02 to 50 ng/mL with a detection limit as low as 3.5 pg/mL. This work provides a promising avenue to develop a high-performance PEC sensing platform based on BIEF as a signal modulation mechanism for clinical diagnostics.
